newsitem.title: FRANCE: For sale -- France's only private glacier.
newsitem.headline: For sale -- France's only private glacier.

text.p: For sale, France's only privately-owned glacier. Pristine Alpine views, eagles and deer, no noisy human neighbours. Price: 5.0 million francs ($880,000).

Frustrated for 30 years, owners of the Gebroulaz glacier in the Alps are making a new push to sell their icy valley near the ski resorts of Meribel and Val Thorens despite a state ruling in 1990 outlawing any new building.
"We think the price is reasonable. For the price of a baguette, you could buy 13 square metres (yards) of the glacier," Marius Fernandez, who represents the family trying to sell, said on Monday.

But the state estimates that the glacier, an Alpine pasture with hunting, three chalets and a small lake is worth just half the asking price, or 2.5 million francs. The area includes chamois deer, eagles and some rare plants.
"Setting a price is very difficult, because there is no market for glaciers," said Yves Brugiere, of the adjoining Vanoise Park which now rents the area for 40,000 francs a year ($7,070).

"State finances can't stretch to buying it. There are other priorities," he said. The 1,700 hectare (4,130 acre) zone stretches from 2,100 to 3,580 metres (6,890 to 11,740 ft), and about a quarter of it is covered by the glacier.

Fernandez said he hoped that a generous donor -- like the state electricity utility EDF-GDF, a mountain lovers' association or a rich philanthropist -- will buy the glacier and donate it to the state.
Alternatively, it might interest people who wanted a mountain retreat for hunting or fishing.

He said the family wants to end a 30-year tussle with the state because French inheritance laws meant the number of heirs would jump to 24 people on the death of his father-in-law, aged 98, from a current 15.
"We don't want to cause a rift in the family with an unmanageable number of interests," he said. "We don't want it to become a poisoned gift."
The glacier has been in the family since 1854.

Before that, it was used for mining silver-bearing lead. Gebroulaz is the only glacier in France not owned by the state and Fernandez said he believed it was the only privately-owned glacier in Europe.

The family came close to selling in 1989 when a businessman offered eight million francs ($1.41 million) with a plan to build a conference centre on the land. The state refused a building permit and classified the area as if it were a natural park.
